content.title: About
content.content: Sunflower meal bread is a whole‑grain loaf that incorporates milled sunflower meal (2554) into the dough. Sunflower meal is a by‑product of oil extraction from sunflower seeds and is rich in dietary fiber, B‑vitamins, vitamin E, magnesium and phosphorus. The bread has a dense crumb, a subtle nutty aroma and a golden crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sunflower meal is obtained after pressing oil from sunflower seeds.
It contains over 10 % dietary fiber, making it an excellent source of roughage.
Adding meal to bread boosts its nutritional value without markedly increasing calories.
Sunflower meal is high in phytosterols, which may help lower cholesterol levels.
Bread with meal is often used in diet plans and programs that promote healthy digestion.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports regular bowel movements, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a potent antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium is essential for muscle and nerve function and helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Phytosterols and monounsaturated fats in the meal may contribute to lower LDL‑cholesterol.

items.title: Enriched with B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Sunflower allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sunflower or its meal.

items.title: High fiber content
items.content: Excessive fiber intake can cause bloating, gas and abdominal discomfort.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Sunflower meal contains modest amounts of oxalates, which people prone to kidney stones may need to limit.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sunflower meal bread works well for sandwiches, toast, serving alongside soups and salads. It can be toasted, crumbled into casseroles, or used as a base for breadcrumbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or cloth sack. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator in an airtight container to prevent drying out and mold growth.
